title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition: the real science this concept draws on. Cities grow in patterns studied by urban science — scaling laws (bigger cities are denser and more productive per capita), network models of streets and transit, and resource-flow accounting. Planets form by accretion: dust grains stick into pebbles, pebbles into planetesimals, planetesimals into planets, over millions of years in a protoplanetary disk — the core-accretion model, supported by exoplanet surveys. This edition records the established science. The ability-crystal concept itself — creating cities and planets through crystal abilities — is a Signature concept and lives in the Signature twin, labeled speculative.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Urban science: how cities really grow
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. Real cities follow measurable laws: Bettencourt-West scaling shows socioeconomic outputs (patents, wages) scale superlinearly with population (~1.15 power) while infrastructure scales sublinearly (~0.85) — bigger cities do more with less per person. Street networks, transit graphs, and utility flows are modeled as networks with known statistics. Urban planners use these models to site districts, size utilities, and predict growth. Any city-creation concept must respect these laws or explain why it beats them.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Planetary formation: the accretion story
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. Planets assemble from dust: micron grains coagulate (sticking by electrostatic and van der Waals forces), grow to pebbles and boulders, then gravity takes over — planetesimals collide and merge, and a core above ~10 Earth masses captures gas to become a giant. The solar system's architecture and thousands of exoplanets constrain the models. Timescale: millions of years. Energy: gravitational and radiogenic. This is the reality any planet-creation proposal must address.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Ability crystals: the Signature concept
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. What exists today that rhymes with the concept: self-assembling materials (DNA origami, block copolymers, and metal-organic frameworks that build ordered structures from programmed parts), 3D-printed buildings (real houses printed layer by layer), and modular construction (city blocks assembled from factory modules). These are the proven stepping stones. The full ability-crystal concept — crystals that direct matter assembly at city and planetary scale — is not established technology and is not presented as such.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — City creation: the lattice-city proposal
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. Planned cities are real: Brasília, Canberra, and Shenzhen were designed before being built, with mixed but instructive results — top-down plans meet bottom-up life. Construction at city scale uses the methods in the construction databases: foundations, utilities, transport, phased occupancy. Any lattice-city proposal inherits this entire body of practice; the crystal concept changes the construction method, not the city's human requirements.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Planet creation: the seeded-accretion proposal
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. Terraforming concepts (warming Mars, thickening atmospheres) are studied seriously and remain centuries-scale projects; moving planets or building them is far beyond current capability. The honest statement: humanity cannot create planets today. Proposals live in simulation and science fiction — valuable for clarifying what would be needed (energy budgets in the 10^32-joule range for Earth-mass assembly, timescales of millennia at best).

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — Resource flows and energy budgets
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. Real megaprojects account mass and energy: a city needs ~10^7 tonnes of material and gigawatt-years of energy; a planet needs 10^24 kg and 10^32 joules. These numbers are the sanity check on every proposal. The database's demos compute budgets for the Signature concept at multiple scales so the claims stay numerical — a proposal with numbers can be argued with; one without cannot.

title: Crystal Ability City and Planet Creation — The concept development path
body: Public edition. Public science and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Public edition. How real concepts mature: simulation first (agent-based city models, N-body accretion codes — both established tools), then laboratory demonstrators (self-assembling materials at bench scale), then field pilots (a grown pavilion, a guided-assembly structure), and only then scale claims. This database follows that path: every Signature record links to a simulation demo, and no record claims a built city or planet. The concept earns credibility one verified step at a time.
